## 1. Start here — one path to a form

**ReFormer MCP — start-here guide**

**Write `<dir>/form.intent.json`, then `form_build {"dir":"<dir>"}` compiles, checks and writes the
module. Never write the module files yourself.**

### The path

1. `form_build {"grammar":"base"}` — the grammar of the intent. Sections on demand: `behavior`,
   `arrays`, `wizard`, `cross`, `async`, `parts`, `operators`, `nodes` (or `all`). Needs no project.
2. Write `<dir>/form.intent.json` with your own file tools. From a markdown spec,
   `plan_form {"specPath":"…","dir":"<dir>"}` writes a draft to finish (never over an existing file).
3. `form_build {"dir":"<dir>"}` cross-checks the intent, type-checks the module and writes every
   file — or nothing while errors remain. Fix the intent on ✗; the form is done on ✓. `dir` is
   relative to the working directory, `form` by default; at a monorepo root pass a folder inside an app.
4. `"target"` keeps the stack, the contract is the same for all three: `core` — you write the JSX
   markup in `index.tsx` (form_build keeps it and type-checks it); `renderer-react` — `FormRenderer`
   over the TS schema; `renderer-json` — the schema as a JSON document plus a registry.

A large form goes in parts: fields + `layoutRoot` → build → validation → build → behavior → build.

### What form_build writes

A flat module with the same names on every target: `model.ts`, `form.schema.ts`,
`form.validation.ts`, `form.behavior.ts`, optional `form.flow.ts` (wizard steps) and
`form.messages.ts` (messages by rule code), `registry.ts` (renderer-json), `data-sources.ts`,
`index.tsx` (the assembly; your markup on core). Yours from the start: `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the
bodies in `operators.ts`. A generated file you edit by hand is detached — the build stops rewriting
it; delete it to bring it back. Test ids come from field paths (`personalData-lastName`).

### Your own code

What the grammar cannot express — own rules and operators (`operators.ts`), loading and submit
(`api.ts`), the markup on core — is code against the library contract:

- `createModel<T>()` is the source of truth; ONE schema tree binds a node by `model: model.$.field`;
- ONE assembly — `createForm({ model, schema, behavior, validation })` inside `useFormBundle`;
- ONE behavior — `defineFormBehavior(({ model, form, schema }) => …)`; validation —
  `defineValidation(({ model }) => …)` with rules from `@reformer/core/validators`, a `{ code }` each;
- checks and submit go through the bundle: `bundle.validate()`, `bundle.submission.submit(handler)`.

### Tools

| Need                                                   | Tool                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| build a form; the intent grammar                       | `form_build`                                      |
| a draft intent from a markdown spec                    | `plan_form`                                       |
| which of two similar operators                         | `choose_api`                                      |
| context for one step of your own code                  | `get_context`                                     |
| signature and example of a symbol                      | `get_symbol_docs`                                 |
| a worked recipe (`wizard`, `form-array`, `json-schema`) | `find_recipe`                                    |
| docs by words / the API surface                        | `search_docs` / `list_symbols`                    |
| check own code, file names, behaviors, a JSON schema   | `validate_form` (`code`, `layout`, `behaviors`, `json-schema`, `bundle`) |
| report a problem of the server                         | `report_issue`                                    |

Prompts: `start-here`, `create-form` (from a description), `plan-form` (from a spec file),
`add-feature` (`validation` | `behavior` | `array` | `wizard`), `to-renderer`, `review`,
`discover-context`.

### Resources

- `reformer://docs/mcp` — the full self-doc of this server: every tool, prompt and resource in detail.
- `reformer://docs/<package>[/<section>]` — library docs: `core`, `cdk`, `ui-kit`, `renderer-react`,
  `renderer-json`, `form-registry`.
- `reformer://catalog` — every section as `[slug, title]`; `search_docs` returns ready URIs.
- `reformer://status` — which packages the server found, their indexes, whether it can type-check.
  Read it when docs come back empty or a tool reports an environment problem.

## 2. get_context

**Tools**

Callable tools exposed by the server (use ListTools to enumerate at runtime). Names and
arguments are exact.

Assembled context for ONE step of work: operator + signature + a canonical example + rules,
anti-patterns and links, deduplicated and cut to a budget.

- `task` (string, required) — the task in your own words, in English or Russian.
- `topics` (string[], optional) — topic ids from `reformer://catalog`; without them the topics are
  inferred from the task.
- `target` (string, optional) — `core` | `cdk` | `ui-kit` | `renderer-react` | `renderer-json`.
- `profile` (string, optional) — `minimal` (~400 tok) | `implementation` (default, ~1000)
  | `debug` (~1800, anti-patterns ahead of the example) | `full` (no ceiling).
- `maxTokens` (number, optional) — a hard ceiling, overrides the profile.

**For a pointed "which API does this" question `choose_api` is cheaper and sharper.** This is
measured, not assumed: as the ONLY call `get_context` gives 69.6% first-pass against 95.7% for
`choose_api` plus a pointed search, at twice the cost per task. `get_context` helps when you need the
context of a whole step at once, or a hard token ceiling.

The shape of the answer shows its confidence: when no rule matched and no symbol is confirmed by the
sections found, there is no `## API` block — the answer says so and leads with sections instead. An
empty block is safer than a confident guess.

## 3. choose_api

Which ReFormer operator meets a requirement stated in your own words. It answers the question the
docs search does not: **which of two similar ones** — `computeFrom` vs `copyFrom`, `copyFrom` vs
`syncFields`, `enableWhen` vs `hideWhen`, `resetWhen` vs `enableWhen`, `validateWhen` vs
`enableWhen`, `resetWhen` vs `onChange`.

The last pair is about the trigger, and it is confused most often. `resetWhen` holds by a
**condition** ("while the payment method is not a card"), while "clear the field when the controlling
one changed" is the **fact of a change**, that is `onChange`. Clearing an array is `onChange` too:
`ModelArray` has its own `.clear()`, and `resetValue` does not apply to it.

- `requirement` (string, required) — ONE requirement, in English or Russian. E.g. "field B is
  available only when A is filled", "total = price \* quantity", "confirmPassword must match
  password".
- `target` (string, optional) — `core` | `renderer-react` | `renderer-json`; narrows the fallback
  search when no rule matched.

Returns the recommended symbol with its signature, a canonical example, why it fits, when it does
NOT, and the anti-patterns the docs record for that substitution. Deterministic: the same requirement
gives the same answer. Each answer also says how the operator is written in `form.intent.json`.

Measured on the eval corpus (46 tasks): with `choose_api` as the first step first-pass went from
80.4% to 95.7%, median tokens per task from 916 to 299, and no task was left unsolved.

## 4. get_symbol_docs

Full JSDoc for one public symbol of any `@reformer/*` package: description, signature,
params, `@returns`, every `@example`, source path.

- `symbol` (string, required) — e.g. `"createForm"`, `"validateModel"`, `"FieldArray"`.
- `package` (string, optional) — e.g. `"@reformer/core"`; omit to search all.

Use before writing code against an unfamiliar symbol.

## 5. find_recipe

A worked example / how-to for a scenario. Cascade: docs/llms filename → `##` section →
symbol `@example` → **full-text search** (same index as `search_docs`) → fallback list.
An unknown topic is no longer a dead end: it comes back as ranked `reformer://docs/…`
candidates with snippets, and the top hit is inlined when it matches a section heading.

- `topic` (string, required) — keyword. Aliases resolve intuitive terms: `wizard`→multi-step,
  `form-array`→arrays, `cycle`→cycle-detection, `copy`→copy-from, `sync`→sync-fields (value
  propagation between fields — a **behavior**), and the validation contract:
  `validate`/`validation`/`cross`/`cross-field`/`validate-async`/`validate-when`→`validation`
  (the `validate`/`validateAsync`/`validateWhen`/`cross`/`apply`/`applyEach` operators + the external
  `validateModel(model, schema)` runner), `json-schema`, `unified-contract` (the contract of a form in
  one place: one schema, one assembly, one behavior), etc.
- `package` (string, optional).

Use to copy a correct pattern instead of guessing.

## 6. search_docs

Full-text search across every documentation section of all `@reformer/*` packages — for when
you can't name the symbol or recipe topic but can describe the task in words. Returns ranked
sections with their `reformer://docs/<pkg>/<slug>` resource URI + a matched snippet; read the
URI to get the full section.

- `query` (string, required) — e.g. `"conditional required validation"`, `"reset form after submit"`.
- `package` (string, optional) — one package or `*`.
- `limit` (number, optional) — default 10, max 25.

Reach for `find_recipe` (curated topic→recipe) or `get_symbol_docs` (one symbol) when you
already know the topic or name; `search_docs` is the fallback when you don't.

## 7. list_symbols

The API surface by kind and package — discovery when you don't know a name.

- `kind` (optional) — `function` | `class` | `interface` | `type` | `const` | `enum`.
- `package` (optional) — one package or `*`.
- `nameContains` (optional) — case-insensitive substring of the symbol name (e.g. `"validate"`,
  `"FileUpload"`). Strongly recommended: the unfiltered surface is 800+ symbols.

E.g. all functions of `@reformer/core` enumerate every validator and behavior. Then
`get_symbol_docs` the one you want.

## 8. validate_form

One door to every check of a form. The kind of check is the `kind` argument; the result always has
one shape: `RF0xx` diagnostics with the place, what to do and a ready next call.

- `kind: "code"` — generated TypeScript. Catches what `tsc` does not see: an unknown `@reformer/*`
  symbol (`RF002`, with similar names), an import from the wrong package OR the wrong subpath
  (`RF003` — `validate` lives only in `@reformer/core/validation`), a validation or behavior
  operator outside its schema (`RF004`/`RF005` — the rule is just not registered, and the field
  silently goes unvalidated), `@deprecated` and removed API of the previous form contract (`RF010`):
  the factories `createCoreForm` / `createReactForm` / `createJsonForm`, the hooks `useReactForm` /
  `useJsonForm`, `JsonFormRenderer`, the node keys `value:` / `array:`, the operator `each`,
  `makeValidationConfig`, the field `renderBehavior` — with the replacement named and the recipe
  `find_recipe unified-contract`.
- `kind: "json-schema"` — a schema document (JSON DSL): node structure, operator syntax, unknown
  component and data-source names. The document is of format 2 (`"format": 2`: key `model`,
  dictionary `parts`, operator `$part`); a document of the previous format gets one error advising
  `migrateJsonSchema`; an object without `format` and `root` (a JSON Schema of the data, a FormIntent)
  is named as "not a form document".
- `kind: "behaviors"` — cycles in computed fields (`RF006`), from the declared `{ target, reads[] }`.
- `kind: "bundle"` — `intent` (an object or a JSON string) is judged the way the build judges it,
  one verdict: problems reading a record (`RF014`, with the nearest key), the C1–C13 cross-checks
  (every `$model` exists in the model, every `$component` is registered, every `$part` is declared,
  every rule target exists, visibility selectors are in the schema, steps are not mixed with other
  nodes — C13), a field outside the layout, a lost issue text, a component not from the kit
  (`RF008`), rules the target does not run (`RF016`: visibility on core). `schema` is optional:
  without it the intent is checked against the schema the build would make.
- `kind: "layout"` — the NAMES of the form module files against the canon (`files[]` + `target`).
  One set for every target; files of the previous contract (`form.render.ts`, `wizard.tsx`,
  `renderer.*`, `validation.ts`) are warnings that say where to move their content.

The limits of the check are printed ALWAYS, a clean report included: "no errors" must not read as
"the code is right" — the parse is line-based, without a TypeScript AST (a deliberate choice:
`typescript` weighs 23 MB and is not a required dependency).

The former `validate_json_schema` and `check_behaviors` are replaced by this tool and removed in 7.0.

## 9. plan_form

A markdown spec → a draft `<dir>/form.intent.json` on disk. The answer is a short summary — what
was parsed (fields, steps, arrays, rules) and what to finish by hand; the intent itself is not
printed, so a large JSON never passes through the model twice. An existing intent file is never
overwritten.

- `specPath` (string, required) — the spec, absolute or relative to the working directory.
- `dir` (string, optional) — the form folder, as in `form_build` (default `form`; required at a
  monorepo root).
- `target` (string, optional) — `core` | `renderer-react` | `renderer-json`.

The parse is heuristic and says so: field types without a type column are guessed by name; formulas
of computed fields and visibility rules are not extracted. A free-text description is no longer
parsed — it gave an empty draft: write the intent by the grammar instead.

## 10. form_build

The one way to make a form: a module on disk from one file, `<dir>/form.intent.json`. You write and
edit only that file with your own Write/Edit; `form_build` compiles it, cross-checks it, type-checks
the module and writes every module file itself, answering with diagnostics only. Nothing is written
while errors remain. There is no `form_build` in the browser worker — it has no disk.

`generate_form` of 6.x, which printed the files for the agent to write by hand, is removed in 7.0,
and so are the aliases `validate_json_schema` and `check_behaviors` (use `validate_form`).

- `dir` (string, optional) — the form folder relative to the working directory, `form` by default;
  required at a monorepo root (a `package.json` with `workspaces`): the default would put the form
  outside every app.
- `grammar` (string, optional) — return the intent grammar instead of building: `base`, a section
  (`behavior`, `arrays`, `wizard`, `cross`, `async`, `parts`, `operators`, `nodes`), several
  comma-separated (`base` may be one of them: `base,arrays` is the base and the section), or `all`.
  `components` lists the kit components by purpose (fields and containers, for a form or a page);
  `components:Card,Tabs` describes each — role, import, parts and props with types, values and the
  kit's descriptions. Needs neither a project nor an intent file.

Without an intent file the call answers with the base grammar. Built files start with the mark
`// @reformer-form-build`; a file edited by hand is detached — the build leaves it alone and says
so. `types.ts` and `api.ts` belong to you. `index.tsx` is built on every target: on `core` it is a
stub with samples — a field, visibility in JSX, `bundle.submission.submit`, steps — kept in step
with the intent until you write your markup there; a renderer target replaces an untouched stub with
its assembly and refuses to keep markup written by hand. Details — `06-form-directory-layout`,
section «`form.intent.json`».

A finding is one line: `<code> at <place>: <what is wrong> → <what to do>`. An unknown key of a
record is an error (`unknown-key`, with the nearest key); a component prop written next to the field
(`placeholder`, `min`) is moved into `componentProps` with a note. The verdict is the one of
`validate_form kind="bundle"`; on top of it the build type-checks the module (a type error says
which file to fix) and needs the environment: `@reformer/core` and `@reformer/ui-kit` installed in
the project.

The lines of the answer, in order (tools and test harnesses parse them — the format is fixed by a
test):

| Line                                                                              | When                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `⚠️ form_build: nothing built — <why>. <next call>`                               | first line when nothing was built and the grammar follows: `<dir>/form.intent.json` does not exist (a `form.intent.json` found above the folder is named), or `grammar` came together with `dir` |
| `✗ form_build: <what> — nothing written.`                                         | first line of a refusal; `<what>` — `form.intent.json is not read in full`, `N errors`, `the environment`, `wrong imports`, …                                                                    |
| `- <finding>`                                                                     | under a refusal: at most 12 findings                                                                                                                                                             |
| `… and N more.`                                                                   | after the 12th finding, or after the 20th warning                                                                                                                                                |
| `✓ form_build: written N, unchanged M. Fields F, arrays A, rules R, behaviors B.` | first line of a success                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Types checked, no errors.`                                                       | second line: the module type-checked clean                                                                                                                                                       |
| `⚠️ Types NOT checked: <reason>. …`                                               | second line instead: nothing to check with (no `typescript`); not "no errors"                                                                                                                    |
| `Folder <path>: <files>.`                                                         | the module folder and its files                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `⚠️ …`                                                                            | reminders: no markup yet on core, operator stubs, files edited by hand that the build no longer produces                                                                                         |
| `Edited by hand and left as is: <files>. …`                                       | files detached from the build                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Warnings: N.`                                                                    | then `- <warning>` lines, at most 20                                                                                                                                                             |

## 11. report_issue

Record a ReFormer problem + its fix as a JSON report on disk — one file per report,
`<project root>/.reformer/issue_reports/<timestamp>-<slug>.json`.

- `error` (string, required), `solution` (string, required), optional `tags`, `context`.

The directory is configurable via the `REFORMER_ISSUE_REPORTS_DIR` env var — an absolute path;
a leading `~` expands to the home directory, a relative value is refused with a text answer. Project root = nearest `package.json` with dependencies above
cwd, searched from outside `node_modules` (an npx run from `node_modules/@reformer/mcp` still writes
to the app); when there is none, reports land in cwd itself. The default `.reformer/` gets its own
`.gitignore`, so reports never reach your commits.

Use when you discover and fix a non-obvious ReFormer error, to help future runs.

## 12. Guided profile (`REFORMER_SURFACE=guided`)

A surface for small local models: the server plans the work and builds; the model only sends
small edits. It lists four tools — `form_start`, `form_edit`, `form_status`, `form_build` — and
no reference tools. Every answer ends with `Next:` — one exact call — until `Done`.

`REFORMER_SURFACE=code-guided` puts the same API inside Code Mode — one `run_script` tool, the
functions are `reformer.formStart`, `reformer.formEdit`, `reformer.formStatus`,
`reformer.formBuild`. The `Next:` lines come as code (`await reformer.formEdit({…})`); a script
that prints nothing gets the answer of its last call. Its `run_script` has its own TypeScript
declaration: `edits: Edit[]`, where `Edit` is a union by `op` with a doc line on every key, the
answer layout under `@returns` and `@example` calls; the preamble says the server writes every file
of the form folder. A call there does not throw: a failed build after applied edits is an answer
with `✗ form_build`, not a script error. The plain Code Mode surface is unchanged.

The form files belong to the server. `form.intent.json` written by hand is put back to the last
version the server wrote (or removed, if the server has not written one yet) before `form_edit`,
`form_status` and `form_build` read it; module files written by hand are rebuilt. Build answers
speak in edits: a type error points to the edit that fixes it, without file names or a file
list. `form_build` with no plan and no form leads to `form_start` instead of the grammar.

- **`form_start`** `{dir?, target, task? | specPath?, formName?}` — plans the stages from the
  task words or the spec (fields; rows, steps, validation, cross-field rules, reactions as
  needed; markup on core) and saves them to `<dir>/form.plan.json`. With `specPath` and no intent
  yet, it drafts `form.intent.json` from the spec as `plan_form` does. A task that names a `.md`
  file the server can read (as written or inside `dir`) gets it as `specPath`.

  **A form already in `dir`** (an intent and no plan, or a plan of a change): the task changes it.
  The plan is one stage `edit`: the changes with `form_edit`, then `confirm: "edit"` after a check
  of the changes — what was added, removed or renamed since the start and what the task names in
  backticks or parentheses (`` `phone` ``, `(phone)`) or as steps in «…»: still there, missing,
  renamed. The checks of a new form (numbers, labels, lost fields) do not run on a change.

- **`form_edit`** `{dir?, edits}` — flat edits; the server writes `form.intent.json` and runs the
  same build as `form_build` (the answer holds its `✓`/`✗ form_build` lines). Edits apply one by
  one: a rejected edit says how to fix it, the others still apply; `"edits":[]` only builds.

  | op                            | Keys                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `add_field`, `set_field`      | `name`, `label`, `type` (string number boolean date), `options`, `mask`, `initialValue`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `component`, `step`; `set_field` with `array` — a row field             |
  | `remove_field`                | `name` — a field, an array or a group; also drops its rules and names the rules of other fields that still read it                                                                          |
  | `rename_field`                | `name`, `to`, `label` — rewrites rules, behaviors (targets, sources, `expr`), conditions, visibility and the layout                                                                         |
  | `rename_step`, `remove_step`  | `title` (or number), `to`; `remove_step` drops the step with its fields, rules and behaviors                                                                                                |
  | `add_array`, `add_item_field` | `name`, `label`, `minItems`, `maxItems`; `array`, `name`, `label`, `type`. A plan without rows refuses `add_array` once; the same call again adds the stage                                 |
  | `add_step`, `place`           | `title`, `fields`; `name`, `step` (number, title or selector)                                                                                                                               |
  | `add_rule`                    | `field`, `array`, `required` `email` `phone` `url` `integer` (true), `min` `max` `minLength` `maxLength` (numbers), `pattern`, `rule`, `cross`, `equals` (another field), `when`, `message` |
  | `remove_rule`                 | `field`, `rule` — one validator; without it every rule of the field                                                                                                                         |
  | `add_behavior`                | `kind` (a core operator), `target`, `expr`, `array`, `when`, `resetOnDisable`; `sources` come from `expr`; the same behavior of the field is replaced                                       |
  | `remove_behavior`             | `target`, `kind` — one kind; without it every behavior of the field                                                                                                                         |
  | `add_visibility`              | `field` or `fields`, `showWhen` or `hideWhen` — renderer targets only                                                                                                                       |
  | `set_form`                    | `formName`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
  | `markup`                      | core only: the server writes JSX in `index.tsx` and keeps it in step with later edits                                                                                                       |

  The server fills what it knows: the component by type, rule codes when a `message` is given,
  `sources` from the expression, the target from the plan. It also reads the usual slips: a
  check written on the field becomes its rule, a mask also gets its format check, `min`/`max` of
  a text are its length, a hand-written email pattern is `email`, choices written
  `value — label` are split, a rule of a field shown on a condition is checked only while shown,
  numbers of a formula are made null-safe. A name in `expr` or `when` that is not a field is
  rejected with the list of fields.

- **`form_status`** `{dir?, skip?, add?, confirm?}` — the stages, the last build, the next
  call. `skip` drops a stage the task does not need (validation is not skipped when the form has
  rules or the task names checks; behavior — when the task has a formula or a field shown on a
  condition), `add` adds one it needs, `confirm: "validation"` closes the check of the form
  against the task, `confirm: "edit"` — the check of a change.

A stage is done by the content of the intent, not by the model's word; `Done` needs a passing
build on the current files with types checked. Validation ends with a check against the task: the
answer shows the task, the fields and the rules, and names what differs — an input the task names
`(name)` with no field, a field the task calls required with no `required` rule, a field the task
shows on a condition with no visibility, a number of the task no rule uses (numbers of a formula
and list markers do not count), a bound the task does not name, a mask not in the task's format, a
default of the task without `initialValue`, labels not in the task's language — with a ready
`form_edit` call where it can be derived. The first `confirm` with differences is refused; a second
one is accepted.

---

_A `debug` tool exists only when the server runs with `REFORMER_DEBUG=true`; ignore it in normal use._

## 13. start-here

**Prompts**

Workflow prompts. Each returns an instruction message for one step: what to write in
`form.intent.json`, which grammar section to ask for, when to call `form_build`.

> **Prompts are a human channel, and most agent clients do not expose them.** If you are an
> agent, check first: without a way to list or invoke prompts, none of this section is reachable
> for you — and there is no error to tell you so. Every prompt below names its tool equivalent;
> use that instead. This is not a fallback, it is the supported path for tool-only consumers.

| Prompt                        | Tool-only equivalent                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start-here`                  | read the resource `reformer://guide`                                        |
| `discover-context`            | read `reformer://status`; `get_context` with your task and `target`          |
| `plan-form`                   | `plan_form {specPath, dir}`, then finish the draft and `form_build`         |
| `create-form`                 | `form_build {"grammar":"base"}`, write the intent, `form_build {dir}`       |
| `add-feature` / `to-renderer` | the grammar section of the feature, edit the intent, `form_build {dir}`     |
| `review`                      | `validate_form` — `kind: "layout"`, then `code` / `behaviors` / `json-schema` |

No arguments. The one path to a form (grammar → `form.intent.json` → `form_build`), where your own
code goes, and the map of tools, prompts and resources.

**Tool-only equivalent:** the resource `reformer://guide`.

## 14. discover-context

- `description` (required), `projectPath` (optional).

Detects the stack of the project (ui-kit, Tailwind, which renderer) and recommends a target.
Optional first step when the target isn't given.

## 15. plan-form

- `specPath` (required), `target` (optional: core | renderer-react | renderer-json), `projectPath` (optional).

Summarises the spec — steps, fields, conditional and computed fields, arrays, API — and leads
through `plan_form` (a draft intent on disk), finishing the draft against the spec, and
`form_build` until ✓.

## 16. create-form

- `description` (required), `target` (optional, default core), `projectPath` (optional).

A new form from a description: the detected stack, the grammar sections to ask for, the intent,
`form_build`, and what is left to you on the chosen target (the JSX markup on core).

## 17. add-feature

One capability for a form built with `form_build`, chosen by `feature`:

- `validation` — rows of `validation` (sections `cross`, `async` when needed);
- `behavior` — records of `behavior` and `visibility` (`choose_api` per requirement);
- `array` — a record of `arrays` with row rules and behaviors (section `arrays`);
- `wizard` — a `FormWizard` root with steps (section `wizard`).

Arguments: `requirements` (what to add; for `wizard` — the steps and their fields) and, optionally,
`code` — the current `form.intent.json`.

## 18. to-renderer

Switch the form to `target`: `renderer-react` (default) or `renderer-json` — `"target"` in the
intent and `form_build`; a hand-written `index.tsx` from core is moved out first. Optional `code` —
the current intent.

## 19. review

- `code` (required).

Cross-package review checklist (state setup, integration, anti-patterns) for existing form code.

---

_A `debug` prompt exists only with `REFORMER_DEBUG=true`._

## 20. URI scheme

**Resources**

Documentation the server serves as MCP resources (ReadResource to fetch).

`ListResources` returns only a few entries — the guide, the catalog, the status and one full-docs
URI per package. It deliberately does NOT enumerate the ~343 individual sections: doing so cost every
client ~20 900 tokens at connection time, before any useful work. To discover section URIs use
`reformer://catalog` (a compact JSON map) or `search_docs`, which already returns ready URIs.
Section URIs themselves are unchanged and read exactly as before.

- `reformer://guide` — start here: the one path to a form (`form.intent.json` → `form_build`), what the build writes, the contract for your own code, and which tool or resource to use. Under 6 KB; the resource form of the `start-here` prompt.
- `reformer://status` — `application/json`: which `@reformer/*` packages the server found (where, version, index, docs), whether it can type-check a form, the ui-kit catalog, and what failed to load.
- `reformer://catalog` — `application/json`: every package → its sections as `[slug, title]`. The index for building the URIs below.
- `reformer://docs/<pkg>` — the full `llms.txt` of one library package (every section concatenated).
- `reformer://docs/<pkg>/<section-slug>` — a single `##` section of a package, by slug.
- `reformer://docs/<pkg>/<file>` — one whole `docs/llms` file of a package, by its name without the
  number (`cdk/field-array` → `02-field-array.md`), as `find_recipe` prints it under **Source**.
  A section slug wins when both match.

`<pkg>` is a short name: `core`, `cdk`, `ui-kit`, `renderer-react`, `renderer-json`, `form-registry`, `mcp`.

## 21. Self-documentation (this server)

- `reformer://guide` — the short start: the first section of this self-doc.
- `reformer://docs/mcp` — the whole self-doc in one document (guide + tools + prompts + resources +
  the library contract behind the module).
- Individual sections are addressable, but their slug is derived from the section's H2 heading, not the
  filename. Enumerate exact URIs via `reformer://catalog`. Examples of real slugs:
  `reformer://docs/mcp/form-intent-json-the-source-for-form-build`,
  `reformer://docs/mcp/schema-one-tree-of-nodes`, `reformer://docs/mcp/checklist-before-you-finish`.

## 22. Library docs (the 6 packages)

Each package's sections come from its `docs/llms/*.md`. Discover exact slugs via `reformer://catalog`
or `search_docs`. The examples below are file names, one whole file each:

- `reformer://docs/core` — model, schema, validators, behaviors, arrays, multi-step, common mistakes (~50 sections).
- `reformer://docs/cdk/field-array`, `reformer://docs/cdk/form-navigation` — FieldArray / FormWizard compounds.
- `reformer://docs/ui-kit/form-field-integration`, `reformer://docs/ui-kit/choice-fields` — components.
- `reformer://docs/renderer-react/render-schema`, `reformer://docs/renderer-react/render-behavior` — the schema tree drawn by `FormRenderer`.
- `reformer://docs/renderer-json/json-schema`, `reformer://docs/renderer-json/registry` — JSON DSL + registry.

## 23. How this relates to tools

`find_recipe` reads the same `docs/llms/*.md` directly (with alias resolution) and, when no curated
recipe matches, cascades into the same full-text search `search_docs` uses — so an unknown topic
returns ranked `reformer://docs/…` candidates instead of a dead end. Resources give you the raw
sections when you want to browse or read a whole package. When you know the scenario, `find_recipe`
is faster; when you want the full section text, read the resource.

## 24. 0. Choose who draws the markup

**The contract behind a form module**

**You do not assemble a form by these steps:** `form_build` writes this module from
`form.intent.json` (see the guide). This chapter is the library contract the generated module
follows — read it when you write your own code next to it (the JSX markup on core, own operators in
`operators.ts`, loading and submit in `api.ts`) or review a module.

A form is described ONE way for every way of drawing it: one schema tree, one binding handle
(`model.$.…`), one assembly (`createForm`), one behavior. The single reactive model is the source of
truth. The parts below go in the order a module is put together; each lists the decision, the key
API, and the traps the runtime would otherwise punish. Exact signatures — `get_symbol_docs`, worked
examples — `find_recipe` (start with `find_recipe unified-contract`).

```ts
// model.ts — initial values and templates of new array rows
export const createCreditModel = () =>
  createModel<CreditForm>({
    loanType: 'consumer',
    registrationAddress: blankAddress(),
    properties: arrayOf(blankProperty),
  });

// form.schema.ts — one schema for every way of drawing
export const creditSchema = (model: FormModel<CreditForm>): FormSchemaNode => ({
  selector: 'wizard',
  component: FormWizard,
  children: [
    {
      selector: 'loan', // the id of the step in flow.steps
      component: Step,
      componentProps: { title: 'Кредит' },
      children: [
        { model: model.$.loanType, component: SelectAsync, componentProps: { label: 'Тип' } }, // field
        { model: model.$.registrationAddress, part: address }, // sub-form
        { model: model.$.properties, component: FieldArray, item: property }, // array of sub-forms
      ],
    },
  ],
});

// index.tsx — one assembly, one hook
const credit = useFormBundle(() =>
  createForm<CreditForm>({
    model: createCreditModel(),
    schema: creditSchema, // JSON: schema: creditJson, registry
    behavior: creditBehavior,
    validation: creditValidation,
  })
);
```

| Layer      | field                             | array                                    | sub-form                              |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| schema     | `{ model: model.$.x, component }` | `{ model: model.$.items, item }`         | `{ model: model.$.group, part }`      |
| validation | `validate(model.$.x, rules)`      | `applyEach(model.$.items, itemRules)`    | `apply(model.$.group, groupRules)`    |
| behavior   | `compute(model.$.x, …)`           | `applyEach(model.$.items, itemBehavior)` | `apply(model.$.group, groupBehavior)` |

- **core** — you write the markup in JSX: one `<FormField control={bundle.form.x} />` per field.
- **renderer-react** — `FormRenderer` draws the schema tree (layout + conditional display as data).
- **renderer-json** — the same tree as a JSON document + a component `registry` (string operators).

Steps 1–6 are the same for all three. They differ only in the shape of the schema passed to the
assembly (a builder or a document + `registry`) and in step 7.

## 25. 1. Model — `createModel<T>(initial)`

The model owns all values. Decisions: the data shape as a `type` (NOT `interface` — see
`find_recipe type-safety-recipes`), and full initial values.

- Numbers optional → `null`; strings → `''`.
- An array of sub-forms is declared together with the template of a new row: `arrayOf(blank, items?)`.
  «Add» is then `model.items.push()` with no argument. The template returns the FULL element with
  plain values. An array that is the value of one field (a multi-select) is just `[]`.
- Export a factory (`createMyModel`), one model per assembly. Don't create it with `useMemo` in a
  component: the assembly in step 3 lives inside `useFormBundle` (a lazy `useState`).

```ts
import { arrayOf, createModel } from '@reformer/core';
type RegForm = { email: string; password: string; age: number | null; phones: Phone[] };
const blankPhone = (): Phone => ({ number: '', kind: 'mobile' });
export const createRegModel = () =>
  createModel<RegForm>({ email: '', password: '', age: null, phones: arrayOf(blankPhone) });
// model.email (value) · model.$.email (binding handle) · model.get() · model.set(full)
```

## 26. 2. Schema — one tree of nodes

ONE schema: a field is described once and stands right where it is drawn. The schema is a builder
`(model) => node`; a node is bound to the model by the key `model` and the handle `model.$.…` —
**binding + display only, no validators**.

| Node      | Shape                                                   | Told apart by                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| field     | `{ model, component, componentProps }`                  | has `model`, no `item`/`part` |
| array     | `{ model, item, component, componentProps }`            | `model` + `item`              |
| sub-form  | `{ model, part }`                                       | `model` + `part`              |
| container | `{ component, componentProps, children }`               | has `children`, no `model`    |

```ts
import type { FormModel, FormSchemaNode } from '@reformer/core';
import { Box, Input, Section } from '@reformer/ui-kit';

// a sub-form (part): declared once, receives a sub-model, paths inside are relative to it
const address = (model: FormModel<Address>): FormSchemaNode => ({
  component: Box,
  children: [
    { model: model.$.region, component: Input, componentProps: { label: 'Регион' } },
    { model: model.$.city, component: Input, componentProps: { label: 'Город' } },
  ],
});

export const formSchema = (model: FormModel<MyForm>): FormSchemaNode => ({
  component: Box,
  children: [
    { model: model.$.email, component: Input, componentProps: { label: 'Email' } },
    {
      selector: 'registration',
      component: Section,
      componentProps: { title: 'Адрес регистрации' },
      children: [{ model: model.$.registrationAddress, part: address }],
    },
  ],
});
```

Traps:

- `model: model.$.field` (a handle) — never a string, never the form node `form.field`.
- `model.$.…` is the handle for a field, a group AND an array. Without `$` you only read a value,
  mutate (`model.items.push()`) or pass a sub-model on.
- The keys `value:` / `array:`, the array facade `model.items` in a binding position, a second
  «render schema» describing the same fields — the former contract.
- No `validators:` key on a node — rules live in their own `defineValidation` (step 4).
- Containers are optional: whoever writes the markup in JSX keeps only field nodes in the schema.
- `selector` is a node id for rules of the behavior (step 5), not a model path.

## 27. 3. Assemble — ONE call, `createForm`

The model, the schema tree, the form, the behavior and the validation are built in a single pass.
The call is the same for every way of drawing; a JSON document goes in as `schema` together with
`registry`.

```ts
import { createForm } from '@reformer/core';
import { useFormBundle } from '@reformer/core/react';

const bundle = useFormBundle(() =>
  createForm<RegForm>({
    model: createRegModel(), // or initial: INITIAL
    schema: formSchema, // BUILDER (model) => node; JSON: the document + registry
    behavior: formBehavior, // optional, step 5
    validation: formValidation, // optional, step 4
    flow: formFlow, // optional: the steps of a wizard
  })
);
// bundle = { model, form, render, flow?, validate(), validateStep(id), submission, dispose() }
// bundle.form.email is a node bound to model.$.email; bundle.submission.submit(handler) checks, then sends
```

In React always wrap the factory in `useFormBundle`: it is a lazy `useState` and runs the factory
once, while `useMemo` may drop its cache and rebuild the form, losing typed input.

`createCoreForm`, `createReactForm`, `createJsonForm` and the hooks `useReactForm` / `useJsonForm`
(three factories for three ways of drawing) have been removed. Low-level
`createFormFromModel({ model, schema })` remains public for special cases; `createLegacyForm`
(both overloads) has been removed.

## 28. 4. Validation — `defineValidation`

Validation is its **own ambient schema** — a plain function over the model, imported from
`@reformer/core/validation`, separate from the form schema (step 2) and from the behavior (step 5).
It runs **on demand** (submit / step), not reactively. Never a `validators:` array on a node.

- **Schema**: `defineValidation<T>(({ model, cross }) => { … })`. The body calls bare **operators**
  imported from `@reformer/core/validation` and `cross` taken from the schema argument:
  - `validate(model.$.x, rules[])` — sync value rules.
  - `validateAsync(model.$.x, asyncRules[])` — async rules `(value, { signal }) => Promise<ValidationIssue | null>`;
    the runner awaits them and passes an `AbortSignal` so a superseded request is cancelled. Network failure → return `null`.
  - `validateWhen(() => cond, () => { … })` — conditional branch: rules inside are active when `cond` is true, else their fields are cleared.
  - `cross(model.$.x, (f) => err | null)` — cross-field; a member of the schema argument, not an
    import. `f` is a **snapshot** of the current scope, not `(value, scope, root)`.
  - `apply(model.$.group, groupRules)` — a sub-form: `groupRules` is a `defineValidation<Group>` that receives the sub-model; one set of rules serves several groups.
  - `applyEach(model.$.items, itemRules)` — the same for every element of an array.
  - `apply(...schemas)` — compose schemas over the same model.

  A schema attached with `apply` / `applyEach` has its own scope: `cross` inside it receives the
  snapshot of the group / the row. `each(model.items, …)` and a direct call
  `groupRules({ model: model.group })` are the former contract.
- **Rules** are factories from `@reformer/core/validators` (`required()`, `email()`, `min(50000)`),
  reused as-is, or inline `(value) => ValidationIssue | null`.
- **To the assembly**: `validation: schema`, or — for a wizard — the steps as data
  `flow: { steps: [{ id: <step selector>, rules? }] }` and the rules outside steps as
  `validation: { extras }`. The bundle checks with `bundle.validate()` and
  `bundle.validateStep(id)` (`ValidationResult` with `status`) and sends with
  `bundle.submission.submit(handler)` (`SubmitResult`: the handler runs only when nothing blocks).
- **Runner**: `validateModel(model, schema): Promise<boolean>` — routes each error into its own node,
  clears fields that became valid, cancels a superseded run (returns `false` — fail-closed), and
  returns `true` even when a `severity: 'warning'` error is showing (warnings don't block submit).
  Keep the schema a **stable `const`** (identity keys the stale-run cancellation).

```ts
import { apply, applyEach, defineValidation, validate, validateAsync } from '@reformer/core/validation';
import { email, minLength, required } from '@reformer/core/validators';

const phoneRules = defineValidation<Phone>(({ model }) => {
  validate(model.$.number, [required()]);
});

export const formValidation = defineValidation<RegForm>(({ model, cross }) => {
  validate(model.$.email, [required(), email()]);
  validate(model.$.password, [required(), minLength(8)]);
  // cross-field reads a snapshot of the scope — no scope/root params
  cross(model.$.confirmPassword, (f) =>
    f.confirmPassword !== f.password ? { code: 'mismatch' } : null
  );
  // async — receives { signal }; network failure returns null (never blocks submit)
  validateAsync(model.$.email, [
    async (value, { signal }) => {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/check-email?e=${value}`, { signal });
      return (await res.json()).available ? null : { code: 'email-taken' };
    },
  ]);
  apply(model.$.registrationAddress, addressRules); // sub-form
  applyEach(model.$.phones, phoneRules); // array rows
});
```

Trap: the old `ModelValidator (value, scope, root)` placed in a leaf's `validators` is gone, and
`validateFormModel` → `{ valid, errors }` is replaced by `validateModel` → `Promise<boolean>` that routes
errors into the nodes itself.

## 29. 5. Behavior — the ONLY behavior of the form (optional)

One function, one file (`form.behavior.ts`), one `behavior` field of the assembly. Next to the model
and the form it gets the schema, so links over the model and rules for schema nodes stand side by
side. Everything is imported from `@reformer/core/behaviors`.

```ts
import { apply, applyEach, compute, defineFormBehavior, enableWhen, hideWhen, onComponentEvent } from '@reformer/core/behaviors';

export const formBehavior = defineFormBehavior<CreditForm>(({ model, form, schema }) => {
  const isMortgage = () => model.loanType === 'mortgage';

  // links over the model
  compute(model.$.monthlyPayment, () => computeMonthlyPayment(model)); // reads OTHER fields, writes its own
  enableWhen(model.$.propertyValue, isMortgage, { resetOnDisable: true });

  // rules for schema nodes — addressed by `selector`
  hideWhen(schema.node('mortgage'), () => !isMortgage());
  onComponentEvent(schema.node('wizard'), 'onSubmit', async () => {
    await submitCreditApplication(model.get());
  });

  apply([model.$.registrationAddress, model.$.residenceAddress], addressBehavior); // sub-forms
  applyEach(model.$.properties, propertyBehavior); // array rows
});
```

- Conditions read the **model** (`model.loanType`) in both kinds of rules — one constant serves
  `enableWhen` and `hideWhen`. `form.loanType.value.value` in a condition is the former contract.
- `hideWhen` hides a NODE; the field stays in the model and is still validated. When it must stop
  participating, pair it with `enableWhen` (which of the two — `choose_api`).
- Rules for nodes are executed by `FormRenderer`. When the markup is written by hand in JSX they do
  nothing: visibility, submit and data loading stay in JSX there.
- **Scopes are isolated.** `schema.node(selector)` sees its own scope only: the root behavior — the
  root tree without the contents of array `item`s and sub-form `part`s. A node inside a row or a
  part is addressed from the sub-behavior passed to `applyEach` / `apply`, which receives its own
  `schema`. So two mounts of one part do not conflict.
- A separate behavior for the render layer (`form.render.ts`, the `renderBehavior` field, a factory
  `(form, model, validation) => (schema) => …`) is the former contract.

Trap: **cycles** (`compute(a, () => a)` or `a→b→a`) loop forever. Plan dependencies and run them
through `validate_form kind="behaviors"`; see `find_recipe cycle`.

Bridge to validation (the only overlap between the layers): a behavior can _trigger_ a re-run —
`revalidateWhen([model.$.dep], () => void validateModel(model, schema))`.

## 30. 6. Arrays & Wizard (when needed)

- **Array of sub-forms**: `arrayOf(blank)` in the model + the node
  `{ model: model.$.items, component: FieldArray, item: itemRow }`; `itemRow` is a part
  `(model: FormModel<Item>) => node`. The node needs no `initialValue` — it is only a fallback for
  forms whose model is created from data without code. In JSX use `FieldArraySection` from
  `@reformer/ui-kit` or the `@reformer/cdk` `FieldArray` compound; **key rows by `id`, not index**.
  `find_recipe form-array`.
- **Wizard**: the library `FormWizard` (`@reformer/ui-kit`) as a schema node, steps are its
  `children`: `{ selector: 'loan', component: Step, componentProps: { title, icon }, children }`
  (`Step` from `@reformer/cdk/form-wizard`). A step is linked to its rules by `selector` —
  `flow: { steps: [{ id: 'loan', rules: loanRules }, { id: 'contacts', rules: contactsRules }] }`,
  rules outside steps — `validation: { extras: crossStepRules }`. The wizard takes the form and the
  flow of steps from the assembly itself: no app shim, no `componentProps.steps`, no
  `makeValidationConfig(model)`, no `onInit` + `patchProps({ form, config })`, no wizard ref — all
  of it is the former contract; the behavior navigates with `flow.goTo(id)`. In JSX `FormWizard`
  takes `form`, `flow={bundle.flow}` and `steps` as props. `find_recipe wizard`.

## 31. 7. Draw

The bundle from step 3 goes to whoever draws.

- **core**: `<FormField control={bundle.form.email} />` per field; a wizard takes `form={bundle.form}`
  and `flow={bundle.flow}`.
- **renderer-react**: `<FormRenderer form={bundle} settings={{ fieldWrapper: FormField }} />`
  (`FormRenderer` from `@reformer/renderer-react`). `find_recipe render-schema`.
- **renderer-json**: the tree as a document of format 2 — `{ "format": 2, "parts": { … }, "root": { … } }`
  with string operators `$model(path)` / `$component(Name)` / `$dataSource(NAME)` / `$part(name)`,
  a `defineRegistry` mapping names → components (incl. `FormWizard`, `Step`, `FIELD_WRAPPER`), then
  the same `createForm({ model, schema: document, registry, … })` and `<FormRenderer form={bundle} />`
  — the field wrapper comes from the registry. A document without `"format": 2` is the former format
  (keys `value`/`array`, steps in `componentProps.steps`); `migrateJsonSchema` converts one.
  **Validate the document with `validate_form kind="json-schema"` before rendering**, and in dev
  call `validateFormSchema(document, { registry })` explicitly. `find_recipe json-schema`.
- **Field components**: put the component ITSELF into `component` — `Input`, `InputNumber` (numbers; `Input` has no `type: 'number'`), `InputSuggest`, `SelectAsync` (registry `Select`), `CheckboxWithLabel` (`Checkbox`), `SwitchWithLabel` (`Switch`), `RadioGroupOptions` (`RadioGroup`), `DatePicker`, `FileUploadDropzone` / `FileUploadInput` (no `variant` prop), … A ui-kit control declares its dialect (`checked`/`onCheckedChange`, `onValueChange`, …) as a static adapter, and the field wrapper (`FormField.Control`, the renderer leaf) binds it to the value seam itself. The old `*Field` line (`InputField`, `SelectField`, `CheckboxField`, …) and `withFormControl` were removed without aliases.
- **Raw third-party controls (non-ui-kit)**: add `resolveFieldAdapter(component) => FieldAdapter | undefined` to the renderer `settings` — the renderer maps the value-seam (`value` + `onChange(value)`) to each control's dialect. For your own control you can instead declare the dialect once with `defineFieldControl(Component, { adapter })` from `@reformer/ui-kit/fields`.

### Validation is a separate schema, not part of the form schema

The form schema (a TS tree or a JSON document) describes **binding and layout** and carries no
validators — there is no `$validator(...)` JSON operator by design. Validation is its own
`defineValidation<T>(({ model }) => …)` bound to the same model. So a form keeps **three**
artifacts over one model, the same for every way of drawing: the **schema** (`form.schema.ts`), the
**validation** (`form.validation.ts`) and the **behavior** (`form.behavior.ts`). Schema and rules
stay independent: a layout pushed from the server changes display without touching the rules, and
vice versa.

## 32. Checklist before you finish

1. The model initialises every field; arrays of sub-forms are `arrayOf(blank)`. 2. Nodes are
`{ model: model.$.x, component, ... }` — the key is `model`, no `validators:` on a node. 3. One
assembly: `createForm` in `useFormBundle`. 4. Validation is a separate `defineValidation`
(sub-forms via `apply`, arrays via `applyEach`), passed as `validation`. 5. One behavior
`({ model, form, schema })`, acyclic (`validate_form kind="behaviors"`). 6. Arrays keyed by `id`.
7. A JSON document has `"format": 2` and passed `validate_form kind="json-schema"`. 8. The code
passed `validate_form kind="code"` — it reports keys and factories of the former contract.

## 33. 1. Minimalist (default) — flat, one file per concern

**Form directory layout (core / renderer-react / renderer-json)**

How to organize the files of one form. **Default = minimalist:** a flat set of files — one
`index.tsx` component plus one file per concern; wizard steps live in the root schema or, one
folder per step, in `steps/<slug>/`. **One naming rule and one file set for every target:**
`form.<role>` is a form artifact whose suffix names its role (`form.schema` — the schema of the
form, `form.behavior` — the behavior of the form, `form.validation` — validation); every other
file is plain-named. The set is **identical across `@reformer/core`, `@reformer/renderer-react`,
and `@reformer/renderer-json`** — the contract of a form does not depend on who draws it;
renderer-json adds only `registry.ts`. Scale up to the folder layout (§3) only for large forms.
Use `[form-name]` / `[FormName]` as placeholders.

> **Кратко по-русски.** Раскладка файлов формы (form directory layout) — как назвать файлы формы и
> куда положить каждый из них. Модуль формы — один каталог, и у каждой заботы в нём ровно один
> канонический файл. Правило имён: `form.<роль>` — артефакт формы, суффикс называет роль
> (`schema`, `behavior`, `validation`); остальные файлы без префикса; внутри папки шага
> `steps/<slug>/` имена те же. Схема одна, поведение одно, сборка одна — поэтому набор файлов у
> всех таргетов одинаковый. Имена из §1 — контракт, а не рекомендация. Прежние имена
> (`form.render.ts`, `wizard.tsx`, `renderer.*`, `validation.ts`) — §7. Крупную форму раскладывают
> по папкам — §3.

> **The names in §1 are the contract, not a suggestion.** Do not invent `schema.ts`, `behavior.ts`,
> `json-schema.json`, `render-behavior.ts`, `initial-values.ts` or `dictionaries.ts` — every concern
> below already has exactly one canonical filename. Older example directories in this repository were
> written before this guide and still use the old names; they are references for _content_, never for
> _naming_.

> `form_build` writes the minimalist layout (§5). This guide documents both it and the folders
> scale-up for a module organised by hand.

What files should a form have? Exactly the set below — the same files for every target.
Everything lives in the form module root (no role folders — those are the large-form layout of §3). A single
`index.tsx` holds the assembly; one `form.validation.ts` holds all validation; every other
concern is one file. The only allowed nesting is the optional per-step folder `steps/<slug>/` (below).

**Naming rule:** `form.<role>` = an artifact of the form, the suffix names its role —
`form.schema` (the one schema tree), `form.behavior` (the one behavior: links over the model and
rules for schema nodes), `form.validation` (validation rules); optional `form.flow`, `form.messages`.
Every other file is **plain-named**.
The separator is a **dot**, never a dash and never a collapsed word: `form.behavior.ts`, not
`form-behavior.ts` / `behavior.ts` / `formBehavior.ts`.

**The set — identical in every target:**

```
[form-name]/
├── index.tsx           # entry: ONE assembly — createForm in useFormBundle — and whoever draws
├── types.ts            # form type + field enums + { value, label } option type + constant dictionaries
├── model.ts            # createModel factory + initial values + new-row templates (arrayOf)
├── form.schema.ts      # the schema: ONE tree of nodes — the form is built from it and drawn by it (json: .json)
├── form.behavior.ts    # the ONLY behavior: links over the model + rules for schema nodes
├── form.validation.ts  # ALL validation over the model; wizard: per-step rules exported + { extras }
├── form.flow.ts        # optional, wizard: steps of the flow — [{ id: <step selector>, rules }]
├── form.messages.ts    # optional: issue texts by code — defineIssueMessages({ 'email.required': '…' })
├── data-sources.ts     # options + async loaders (dataSources)
├── api.ts              # submit + prefill / load
└── operators.ts        # optional: own operators — rules, validation and behavior operators
```

**Optional files.** `form.flow.ts` — `formFlow: FormFlowConfig<T>`, steps `[{ id: <step selector>, rules }]`
(rules imported from `form.validation.ts`) → `createForm({ flow })`. `form.messages.ts` — issue texts by
code, `defineIssueMessages({ 'loanAmount.required': '…' })` → `<ValidationMessagesProvider messages>`.
`operators.ts` — the form's own operators (§8).

**`form.schema.*` — one tree, two notations:**

| target         | file               | content                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| core           | `form.schema.ts`   | builder `(model) => node`: `{ model: model.$.x, component, componentProps }`; the markup is JSX |
| renderer-react | `form.schema.ts`   | the same builder, with containers — `FormRenderer` draws the tree                               |
| renderer-json  | `form.schema.json` | the same tree as a document of format 2 (`$model` / `$component` / `$part`), stored as data     |

- **`.tsx` instead of `.ts` is fine** when the schema itself contains JSX (an inline cell
  renderer). Only the extension changes: `form.schema.tsx`, never `schema.tsx` / `json-schema.ts`.
- **renderer-json — why `.json` is the default.** ui-builder opens only `*.schema.json`.
  `index.tsx` imports it: `schemaDocument as unknown as JsonFormSchema<T>` (`resolveJsonModule`).
  `form_build` writes the `$model(...)` paths from the intent and cross-checks them; its mark is
  `meta.description`, and a document saved from ui-builder is a hand edit.
- **`form.schema.ts` is an accepted variant** (renderer-json): the same document in
  `defineJsonSchema<T>` — a `$model` typo fails at compile time, but ui-builder does not open it.

**Behavior — one layer, one file.** `form.behavior.ts` holds `defineFormBehavior<T>(({ model, form, schema }) => …)`:
links over the model (compute / enableWhen / copyFrom / onChange) and rules for schema nodes
(`hideWhen(schema.node('selector'), …)`, `onComponentEvent`, `onMount`) side by side — in **every**
target. There is no separate file for the render layer.

**renderer-json also adds** `registry.ts` (plain) — binds components and the data-sources **from
`data-sources.ts`** to their `$component(...)` / `$dataSource(...)` names, including the library
`FormWizard` / `Step` and the field wrapper `FIELD_WRAPPER`.

**Wizard** is the library `FormWizard` standing in the schema as a node with the steps in
`children` — it needs no file of its own. A step node carries a `selector`; the same word is the
`id` of the step in `form.flow.ts`.

**Wizard steps, optional — `steps/<slug>/`:** keep the steps in the root schema, **or** give each
step a folder named by the kebab slug of its title **without a number** (`Контакты` → `kontakty`;
order comes from the aggregator, so reordering steps never renames folders). Inside a step folder
the names are the same as in the root:

```
steps/
├── index.ts                # aggregator: step order + the step schemas / rules
└── kontakty/
    ├── form.schema.ts      # the step node `{ selector, component: Step, … }` (optional; .tsx / .json as in the root)
    ├── form.validation.ts  # rules of this step's fields → export const stepRules
    └── form.behavior.ts    # behavior within this step (optional)
```

Cross-step rules and behavior stay in the root `form.validation.ts` / `form.behavior.ts`.

A **data** schema (`form.schema.json`, renderer-json) is split by reference: the root keeps
`{ "$ref": "./steps/<slug>/form.schema.json" }` among the wizard's `children`, the step file is
`{ "$schema", "node": <Step> }` (key `node`, not `root`), `steps/index.ts` exports
`stepSchemas: Record<ref, JsonFormStep>`, and `index.tsx` assembles the document with
`composeJsonFormSchema(rawSchema, stepSchemas)` before `createForm`.

→ per-target file sets:

```
core (8):            index.tsx  types.ts  model.ts  form.schema.ts  form.behavior.ts  form.validation.ts  data-sources.ts  api.ts
renderer-react (8):  index.tsx  types.ts  model.ts  form.schema.ts  form.behavior.ts  form.validation.ts  data-sources.ts  api.ts
renderer-json (9):   index.tsx  types.ts  model.ts  form.schema.json  form.behavior.ts  form.validation.ts  data-sources.ts  api.ts  registry.ts

# same names, allowed shapes:
any target                     schema holds JSX        -> form.schema.tsx
renderer-json                  schema typed by tsc     -> form.schema.ts with defineJsonSchema<T>  (ui-builder does not open it)
any target + wizard, optional  steps as folders        -> steps/index.ts + steps/<slug>/{form.schema.*, form.validation.ts, form.behavior.ts}
```

Rules:

- **Wizard steps in the root schema or in `steps/<slug>/`** — never `components/steps/`,
  `step1.tsx` or a numbered folder. A nested sub-form (Address, PassportData, …) is a **part** — a
  function `(model) => node` next to the schema that uses it, mounted with `{ model, part }` — not
  a separate file per sub-form.
- Nodes carry the **model handle** (`model: model.$.x`), never `form.X`; the key is `model`, not
  `value` / `array`.
- Schema nodes carry **no `validators`** — value validation is a separate `defineValidation`
  over the model in `form.validation.ts`, passed to the assembly as `validation`.
- Derived fields and node visibility → `form.behavior.ts`; domain constants/enums → `types.ts`;
  the two data concerns are split: field options + async loaders → `data-sources.ts`,
  submit/prefill → `api.ts`.
- **The set is the whole module.** A concern with no file of its own does not get a new file — it
  belongs inside one of these. The documented exception is the `steps/` folders above.

## 34. 2. App-level infrastructure (renderer-json only) — recommendation, not a conformance bar

> **Status: aspirational.** Nothing in this repository implements the layout below: no example has a
> `src/renderer-json/` directory, and the meta-schema generator is currently wired to one specific
> form. A form that keeps its whole registry in its own `registry.ts` is therefore **not** violating
> the layout — **§1 alone is the conformance bar**, and neither a reviewer nor a validator should read
> a missing `src/renderer-json/` as a defect. Adopt §2 when a second or third JSON form appears in the
> app and the base registry actually starts getting copy-pasted.

The base component **registry** is mostly shared across all JSON forms — ui-kit components plus the
system ones (`FormWizard`, `Step`, `FIELD_WRAPPER`). The DSL meta-schema is generated from that
registry. Neither belongs to a single form — once there is more than one, lift them to the app
level (e.g. `src/renderer-json/`):

```
src/renderer-json/            # one per application
├── registry.ts               # base ComponentRegistry: ui-kit + FormWizard / Step + FIELD_WRAPPER
└── form-schema.schema.json    # GENERATED DSL meta-schema (npm run gen:form-schema) — derived from the registry
```

Once that app-level base exists, each form's own `registry.ts` composes it (`composeRegistries`)
with the form's own components + `data-sources.ts`, and that composed registry goes into
`createForm({ registry })`; from then on do **not** copy the base registry or the meta-schema into
a per-form file — regenerate the meta-schema with `npm run gen:form-schema` when the base registry
changes. Until it exists, a self-contained per-form `registry.ts` is the correct shape, not a
workaround.

> Raw (non-ui-kit) controls are bound by name the same way, but need a `resolveFieldAdapter` in the
> renderer **settings** (see `@reformer/renderer-react`), not in the registry itself.

## 35. 3. Scale up: folders (large forms)

When a form grows large (many steps, sub-forms reused across steps, several ways of drawing), the
flat module becomes **role folders** — the layout of the reference credit application
(`projects/react-playground/src/pages/demo/complex-multy-step-form`). A folder names the role; the
names of the files inside are free:

```
[form-name]/
├── [FormName]Form.tsx   # entry: the markup written by hand (or FormRenderer); index.ts — re-exports
├── model/               # the form type's model: createModel factory, initial values, row factories (arrayOf)
├── schema/              # the schema: root node (form.ts), steps/ (one step node per file), sections/ (parts)
├── validation/          # rules per step + cross-step rules (form.ts → { extras }) + messages.ts (issue texts)
├── behavior/            # the behavior: derived values, conditions, synchronisation, dynamic options
├── flow/                # the steps of the wizard: FormFlowConfig — [{ id: <step selector>, rules }]
├── application/         # assembly (create.ts → createForm), load, submit, payload (input only, no derived)
├── api/                 # requests to the server
├── components/          # markup by hand: steps/, nested-forms/, ui/
├── types/               # value types: the input (sent) and the derived values (computed by the behavior)
└── constants/  utils/  hooks/
```

- `model/` and `schema/` are required, and so is the entry; the other folders appear when the
  form needs them. Every way of drawing (by hand, `FormRenderer`, JSON) shares `model/`, `schema/`,
  `validation/`, `behavior/`, `flow/`; only the entry differs.
- `application/create.ts` is the one assembly: `createForm({ model, schema, behavior, validation,
flow })`. `validation/form.ts` keeps only the rules outside steps (`{ extras }`); the step rules
  go to the flow.
- Types are split into the **input** (what the user fills in and the server receives) and the
  **derived** values (written by `compute`); the form type is their intersection, and the payload
  drops the derived keys before the request.
- `validate_form kind="layout"` recognises this layout by its role folders: it checks the top-level
  folders and the entry, not the file names inside them.

## 36. 4. Scaling

| Complexity               | Structure                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tiny                     | single file: `index.tsx` (model + schema + component)                                                                                                                     |
| **Default (minimalist)** | flat files (§1) — plain-named base + `form.schema` / `form.behavior` / `form.validation`; wizard steps in the root schema or in `steps/<slug>/`; identical across targets |
| Large                    | folders (§3): role folders `model/` `schema/` `validation/` `behavior/` `flow/` `application/` (+ app-level registry/meta-schema for renderer-json)                       |

## 37. 5. Which layout `form_build` writes

`form_build` always writes the flat **minimalist** layout under the canonical names above; the
`folders` layout is for a large module you organise by hand. The former `REFORMER_FORM_LAYOUT`
switch only steered the `create-form` prompt, and the prompt no longer writes modules — it was
removed in `@reformer/mcp` 7.0.

## 38. 6. Reuse map

The contract of a form is the same for every way of drawing, so almost every file is written once.

| File                                | Role                                                                                    |       core        |  renderer-react   |        renderer-json         |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------: | :---------------: | :--------------------------: |
| `types.ts`                          | form type + enums + option type + constants                                             |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `model.ts`                          | reactive model (source of truth) + new-row templates                                    |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `form.validation.ts`                | rules; wizard: step rules exported + `{ extras }`                                       |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `form.flow.ts`                      | wizard: steps of the flow `[{ id, rules }]`                                             | optional (wizard) | optional (wizard) |      optional (wizard)       |
| `form.messages.ts`                  | issue texts by code (`defineIssueMessages`)                                             |     optional      |     optional      |           optional           |
| `form.behavior.ts`                  | the one behavior: model links + node rules                                              |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `data-sources.ts`                   | options + async loaders (dataSources)                                                   |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `api.ts`                            | submit + prefill/load                                                                   |        ✅         |       reuse       |            reuse             |
| `operators.ts`                      | own rules and validation / behavior operators                                           |     optional      |     optional      |           optional           |
| `form.schema.ts`                    | the one schema tree: TS builder; renderer-json — typed document (`defineJsonSchema<T>`) |        ✅         |       reuse       |           variant            |
| `form.schema.tsx`                   | same file when the schema contains JSX                                                  |      variant      |      variant      |           variant            |
| `form.schema.json`                  | the JSON document of format 2 — what ui-builder opens                                   |         —         |         —         |              ✅              |
| `registry.ts`                       | binds components + data-sources to DSL names                                            |         —         |         —         |              ✅              |
| `steps/index.ts` + `steps/<slug>/…` | per-step schema / validation / behavior                                                 | optional (wizard) | optional (wizard) |      optional (wizard)       |
| **app** `registry.ts` (base)        | ui-kit + system components                                                              |         —         |         —         | app-level (§2, aspirational) |
| **app** `form-schema.schema.json`   | generated DSL meta-schema                                                               |         —         |         —         | app-level (§2, aspirational) |

Rule nodes of the behavior (`hideWhen`, `onComponentEvent`, `onMount`) are executed by the renderer.
When the markup is written by hand (core) there is none, so `form_build` refuses them
(`not-on-target`): visibility, submit and data loading are written in the JSX of `index.tsx` there.

Renaming any of these is a defect in itself: the stems above are the contract that reviews, generators
and `find_recipe directory-layout` key on. Older example directories in this repository predate the
contract and are **not** naming references.

## 39. 7. Former names (`form.render.ts`, `wizard.tsx`, `renderer.*`, `validation.ts`)

The canon was aligned twice. First the render layer lost its `renderer.` prefix and validation got
the `form.` prefix. Then the unified contract removed two roles altogether: the separate behavior of
the render layer and the app shim of the wizard. Modules written the old way keep working —
`validate_form kind="layout"` reports these names as **warnings**, never as errors:

| former name                              | now                                                                                                                     | diagnostic |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `renderer.schema.ts`                     | `form.schema.ts` (`.tsx` / `.json` alike) — rename                                                                      | RF011      |
| `validation.ts`                          | `form.validation.ts` (in `steps/<slug>/` too) — rename                                                                  | RF011      |
| `form.render.ts`, `renderer.behavior.ts` | no such file: move the node rules into `form.behavior.ts` (in `steps/<slug>/` — into the step's own `form.behavior.ts`) | RF013      |
| `wizard.tsx`, `renderer.wizard.tsx`      | no such file: the wizard is the library `FormWizard` node; delete the shim                                              | RF013      |

Fix it when you next touch the module; new code uses the canonical names only. `core` and
`renderer-react` share one file set, so the files alone no longer tell these targets apart — pass
`target` to `validate_form kind="layout"` explicitly.

## 40. 8. `form.intent.json` — the source for `form_build`

An optional addition to the module. Author and edit only this file: `form_build` compiles it,
type-checks the result and writes the module. Files it wrote start with a `// @reformer-form-build`
marker. Editing such a file by hand detaches it: the build keeps your version and says so; delete
the file to bring it back. `types.ts` and `api.ts` stay yours. On the `core` target `index.tsx` is
a stub with samples (a field, visibility in JSX, `bundle.submission.submit`, steps) that the build
keeps in step with the intent until you write the JSX markup there; from then on it is yours, and
the build type-checks it. Switching to a renderer target replaces an untouched stub and refuses to
keep markup written by hand.

Own operators are built on the core ones: a rule factory returning `Rule<T>`, a validation operator
over `validate` / `cross` / `validateWhen`, a behavior operator over the `@reformer/core/behaviors`
operators or `effect` + `onDispose`. The intent declares them in `operators` — name → module
(`"./operators"`) — and `form.validation.ts` / `form.behavior.ts` import them like the core ones. For
a module in the form folder the build writes a stub (`operators.ts`): signatures that accept any
arguments, empty bodies, `TODO(form_build)` marks. Until you edit it, the stub follows the intent;
writing the bodies detaches it like any built file, and the build keeps reminding you while marks
remain.

## 41. Package entries

**Embedding — package entries and the browser worker**

How to use `@reformer/mcp` without spawning the CLI server: the package entries for a host
application (an editor, a builder plugin, a test) and the self-contained Web Worker bundle.
An agent that only calls the server's tools does not need this file.

| Entry                 | Contents                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@reformer/mcp`       | the stdio server (`bin`: `reformer-mcp`); not meant to be imported                                 |
| `@reformer/mcp/core`  | `createKnowledge(sources)`, `memoize`; types `Knowledge`, `KnowledgeSources`, `SymbolsFallback`, `UiKitCatalogSource` |
| `@reformer/mcp/browser` | `createBrowserKnowledge(input)` → `{ knowledge, issues }` — knowledge from already loaded data   |
